text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sheila Copps sets stage for war over culture: Heritage Minister pledges to 'play hardball' in defending Canadian interests against U.S. incursions.
- Spread of HIV hits young: Risky sex blamed by Health Canada.
- Yeltsin's ex-aide wins by-election: Gains platform for corruption claims.
- Pedophile alert issued by Toronto schools: Police investigate rash of incidents in which children accosted by man.
- O.J. Simpson must pay C$25-million more: C$33.5-million total damages dwarfs plaintiffs' estimate of ex-football star's worth.
- Tembec bids for Spruce Falls: Offers C$175-million to buy remaining shares of Ontario newsprint producer.
- Explain dropped bid, 88 told: Initial argument 'disingenuous'
- Tip Top tiptoes uptown: The venerable men's wear chain is about to get some 'taste and style' in a bid to win young clients and regain its No. 1 ranking.
- Desjardins fights to stay in insurance: Quebec committee recommends government ban in-branch sales at co-operative.
- Boom times for home buyers and builders.
- MacBlo faces backlash: Several directors will not stand for re-election as disgruntled shareholders and some senior executives show anger over asset writedowns and sizable losses.
